rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they cannot produce a comparable surah, even after claiming success and consulting their witnesses, their denial defies the divinely supported Messenger and warrants fear of punishment.
rows.anchor: أي فإن لم تأتوا بسورة أو أتيتم بما زعمتم أنه سورة ولم يستطع ذلك شهداؤكم على التفسيرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “do” is omitted and supplied from context: bringing a surah like the Qur’an; Ibn Ashur defers comparison with the ellipsis at 5:67.
rows.anchor: ومفعول { تفعلوا } محذوف يدل عليه السياق أي فإن لم تفعلوا ذلك أي الإتيان بسورة مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although failure was expected, conditional in presents it as unlikely to encourage a sincere attempt, exhaust excuses, and draw opponents toward fair-minded debate.
rows.anchor: وجيء بإن الشرطية التي الأصل فيها عدم القطع مع أن عدم فعلهم هو الأرجح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The progression moves from inviting a surah, to asking them to consider possible failure, to declaring their inability, alternating conciliatory encouragement with warning.
rows.anchor: كأن المتحدي يتدبر في شأنهم ، ويزن أمرهم فيقول أولا ائتوا بسورة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh distinguishes lā as negating the present and lan as negating the future.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال سيبويه لا لنفي يفعل ، ولن لنفي سيفعل فقد قال الخليل

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil analyzes lan as a contraction of negative lā and the future particle an; Ibn Ashur calls this a good account.
rows.anchor: فقد قال الخليل إن لن حرف مختزل من لا النافية وأن الاستقبالية وهو رأي حسن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says lan conveys permanent negation, literally or figuratively as emphasis.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري بإفادتها التأبيد حقيقة أو مجازا وهو التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unbounded future negation generally covers all future times; Ibn Ashur’s survey finds lan used for emphatic or permanent negation and rejects grammarians who deny that force.
rows.anchor: وقد استقريت مواقعها في القرآن وكلام العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prediction is miraculous because the challenge should have intensified opposition, yet no contemporary opponent produced a rival despite abundant motives, eloquent talent, and public opportunities.
rows.anchor: { ولن تفعلوا } من أكبر معجزات القرآن فإنها معجزة من جهتين : الأولى أنها أثبتت أنهم لم يعارضوا لأن ذلك أبعث لهم على المعارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also a continuing prophecy: neither the challenged Arabs nor later generations have produced a successful counter to the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: الثانية أنه أخبر بأنهم لا يأتون بذلك في المستقبل فما أتى أحد منهم ولا ممن خلفهم

rows.speaker: ابن العلج
rows.claim: Ibn al-Alj is cited for treating إن and لم as competing to govern the same verb; Ibn Ashur says their meanings differ, so this is not the case here.
rows.anchor: كما توهمه ابن العلج أحد نحاة الأندلس نسبه إليه في ( التصريح على التوضيح )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first تفعلوا is jussive under لم: إن governs the condition after the verb has already been construed as negated by لم.
rows.anchor: لأن ( إن ) الشرطية دخلت على الفعل بعد اعتباره منفيا فيكون معنى الشرط متسلطا على ( لم ) وفعلها

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi’s works support allowing two particles to compete for one complement when their semantic demands agree.
rows.anchor: وقد أخذ جوازه من كلام أبي علي الفارسي في ( المسائل الدمشقيات ) ومن كتاب ( التذكرة ) له

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: A rajaz line pairing the two forms of ka-anna is cited as evidence for particle competition; the poet is unnamed.
rows.anchor: ومن كتاب ( التذكرة ) له أنه جعل قول الراجز :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fear the Fire” stands for omitted conclusions: recognize that Muhammad is truthful, accept God’s oneness and the revelation, and fear punishment if disobedient; recognizing the Messenger entails belief in resurrection.
rows.anchor: لدلالته عليه وإيذانه به وهو إيجاز بديع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compact verb تفعلوا encompasses the challenge’s special conditions—matching the Qur’an and enlisting witnesses—more efficiently than the simpler “bring” in Joseph 12:59–60.
rows.anchor: لأن في لفظ { تفعلوا } هنا من الإيجاز ما ليس مثله في الآية الأخرى إذ الإتيان المتحدى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, waqūd names the material burned as fuel; Ibn Ashur says this is required here because the verse means fuel.
rows.anchor: والوقود بفتح الواو اسم لما يوقد به ، وبالضم مصدر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya records both vowelings for the meanings of firewood and verbal noun; an unnamed view reverses the usual assignment.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية حكي الضم والفتح في كل من الحطب والمصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual pattern faʿūl names what an action is done with; seven exceptional forms occur as verbal nouns, including waqūd.
rows.anchor: وقياس فعول بفتح الفاء أنه اسم لما يفعل به كالوضوء والحنوط والسعوط والوجور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A noncanonical ḍamma reading is construed either as a verbal noun or by ellipsis, “those whose fuel is people and stones.”
rows.anchor: وقريء بالضم في الشاذ وذلك على اعتبار الضم مصدرا أو على حذف مضاف أي ذوو وقودها الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nās refers to the unbelieving class by customary generic definiteness; it may instead be definite by prior covenant, since other verses identify the people as polytheists.
rows.anchor: والناس أريد به صنف منهم وهم الكافرون فتعريفه تعريف الاستغراق العرفي ويجوز أن يكون تعريف العهد

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: The plural ḥijāra is an unusual, nonanalogical plural of ḥajar; Sibawayh compares its feminine ending to forms such as baʿūla and fuʿūla.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه كما ألحقوها بالبعولة والفحولة

rows.speaker: أبو الهيثم
rows.claim: Abu al-Haytham says Arabs add tāʾ marbūṭa to plurals on faʿāl or faʿūl to ease pausing after the final consonant and long vowel.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي الهيثم أن العرب تدخل الهاء في كل جمع على فعال أو فعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stones serve as the Fire’s fuel, burning more intensely and slowly extinguishing; the stones include the idols, as stated explicitly at 21:98.
rows.anchor: ومعنى وقودها الحجارة أن الحجر جعل لها مكان الحطب لأنه إذا اشتعل صار أشد إحراقا وأبطأ انطفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning indirectly threatens the audience with becoming fuel themselves: “people” signals worshippers, while “stones” signals their idols, through two levels of inference.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية تعريض بتهديد المخاطبين والمعنى المعرض به فاحذروا أن تكونوا أنتم وما عبدتم وقود النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Casting idols into Hell humiliates them and exposes their worshippers’ error; their former source of pride and hoped-for rescue becomes a cause of punishment and lasting regret.
rows.anchor: وحكمة إلقاء حجارة الأصنام في النار مع أنها لا تظهر فيها حكمة الجزاء أن ذلك تحقير لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Prepared for the unbelievers” is an independent predication, not a coordinated second modifier; its independent force heightens terror and implies preparation for the interlocutors.
rows.anchor: استئناف لم يعطف لقصد التنبيه على أنه مقصود بالخبرية لأنه لو عطف لأوهم العطف أنه صفة ثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s inimitability is uniquely established by mass transmission: Arabs perceived it directly, later audiences through transmission, and Arabic specialists can also assess it directly.
rows.anchor: فأما القرآن فإعجازه ثبت بالتواتر النقلي أدرك معجزته العرب بالحس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge uses the Arabs’ own letters, words, and rhetorical styles; their inability to match the Qur’an despite talent, collaboration, and powerful motives shows its eloquence exceeds human capacity and confirms revelation.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو رأي جمهور أهل السنة والمعتزلة وأعيان الأشاعرة مثل أبي بكر الباقلاني وعبد القاهر الجرجاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arab tribes’ voluntary, rapid acceptance after Mecca’s conquest is further evidence: once Quraysh’s opposition fell, many strong tribes had no reason to capitulate unless they were already convinced and only pride had delayed them.
rows.anchor: ذلك الدليل هو إسلام جميع قبائل العرب وتعاقبهم في الوفادة بعد فتح مكة فإنهم كانوا مقتدين بقريش في المعارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words “you will never do it” remain a miracle across centuries because no one among the original challengers or their successors has opposed the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: فإنها قد مرت عليها العصور والقرون وماصدقها واضح إذ لم تقع المعارضة من أحد من المخاطبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Non-Arabs can know the miracle by proof even without the Arabs’ immediate linguistic perception; learning Arabic language and literary style lets them approach the same direct appreciation.
rows.anchor: فيكون الإعجاز للعرب بالبداهة ولمن جاء بعدهم بالاستدلال والبرهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial clause answers how disbelief is possible and offers the first proof of God’s existence and power: each person knows they came into being after nonexistence.
rows.anchor: جملة حالية وهي تخلص إلى بيان ما دلت عليه ( كيف ) بطريق الإجمال وبيان أولى الدلائل على وجوده وقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human life emerges through a wondrous sequence: lifeless elements enter food, bodily constituents and gametes, then clot and morsel, before the spirit is breathed and life begins; this should establish God’s exclusive divinity.
rows.anchor: ثم امتزج فصار علقة ثم مضغة كل هذه أطوار أولية لوجود الإنسان وهي موجودات ميتة ثم بثت فيه الحياة بنفخ الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If death means absence of life in a body capable of life, the developing embryo can commonly be called dead before acquiring life; this prepares the sequence of enlivening, death, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق الأموات هنا مجاز شائع بناء على أن الموت هو عدم اتصاف الجسم بالحياة سواء كان متصفا بها من قبل

rows.speaker: أئمة اللغة
rows.claim: Many leading lexicographers, followed by al-Zamakhshari and al-Sakkaki, define death as loss of life after life existed; on this apparent sense, the pre-life “dead” is metaphorical, though Qur’anic usage is familiar either way.
rows.anchor: وقال كثير من أئمة اللغة الموت انعدام الحياة بعد وجودها وهو مختار الزمخشري والسكاكي وهو الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In religious usage life is the spirit’s infusion into a body; philosophers have not given a strict definition, but descriptively it is a power producing sensation and motion under a suitable bodily temperament.
rows.anchor: والحياة ضد الموت ، وهي في نظر الشرع نفخ الروح في الجسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life begins when the body’s balanced composition and vital spirit yield an appropriate temperament; it persists while that order holds and ceases when it breaks down.
rows.anchor: فباعتدال ذلك التركيب يكون النوع معتدلا ولكل صنف من ذلك النوع مزاج يخصه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: A Tirmidhi report from Ibn Masʿud, quoting the Prophet, describes forty days as a drop, then equivalent periods as clot and morsel, after which an angel breathes in the spirit; Ibn Ashur gives no grading.
rows.anchor: حديث الترمذي عن عبد الله بن مسعود أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is nonexistence and life a positive state, and both are created by God, as affirmed in 67:2.
rows.anchor: فالموت عدم والحياة ملكة وكلاهما موجود مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s purpose is proof, not a statement of blessings: it juxtaposes life, which people count as a favor, with the two deaths they do not count as favors.
rows.anchor: الامتنان بل هو استدلال محض ذكر شيئا يعده الناس نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection clause either teaches a conclusion rather than proving it to deniers, or follows from the justice and wisdom of a Creator who would not leave good and evil deeds unrewarded in this life.
rows.anchor: فذلك تفريع عن الاستدلال وليس هو بدليل إذ المشركون ينكرون الحياة الآخرة فهو إدماج وتعليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Return to God is pictured as a traveler’s return home: creation began from God, and resurrection brings people back for judgment and recompense.
rows.anchor: شبه الحضور للحساب برجوع السائر إلى منزله باعتبار أن الله خلق الخلق فكأنهم صدروا من حضرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preposing إليه creates true restriction, informing deniers that return is to God alone and that their idols cannot help them at resurrection.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المتعلق على عامله مفيد القصر وهو قصر حقيقي سيق للمخاطبين لإفادتهم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use the passive, depicting God returning people despite their denial; Yaʿqub reads the verb actively, describing their return without specifying whether it is voluntary or compelled.
rows.anchor: و { ترجعون } بضم التاء وفتح الجيم في قراءة الجمهور ، وقرأه يعقوب بفتح التاء

words: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may be a second proof, escalating from human creation to the many earthly creatures; alternatively it is a favor statement embedding proof of God’s creative power, with لكم marking benefit to people.
rows.anchor: دلائل ربوبية الله ووحدانيته ظاهرة في خلق الإنسان وفي خلق جميع ما في الأرض

words: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The uncoordinated sentence may signal close connection: earthly provisions complete the existence begun in 2:28; alternatively, omitting conjunction shows the first proof stands independently, though Ibn Ashur notes drawbacks to both analyses.
rows.anchor: وفصل الجملة السابقة يجوز أن يكون لمراعاة كمال الاتصال بين الجملتين لأن هذه كالنتيجة للدليل الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is the spherical world of land and sea inhabited by people and containing animals, plants, and minerals; the verse names what is within it because those visible kinds invite reflection.
rows.anchor: والأرض اسم للعالم الكروي المشتمل على البر والبحر الذي يعمره الإنسان والحيوان والنبات والمعادن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse attaches creation to earth’s contents rather than to earth itself, it implies God created the container: the container cannot sensibly be later than its contents or precede them pointlessly.
rows.anchor: فاستفادة أنه خلق الأرض مأخوذة بطريق الفحوى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows “earth” to mean the lower region, parallel to “heaven” as the upper region; Ibn Ashur rejects this because earth literally names the globe and only figuratively a region.
rows.anchor: فمن البعيد أن يجوز صاحب ( الكشاف ) أن يراد بالأرض الجهة السفلية كما يراد بالسماء الجهة العلوية
